notesStmt.note: This manuscript was probably written shortly before Whitman submitted the poem for publication in November 1887.
"Yonnondio" was first published in the 26 November 1887 issue of The Critic. It was later included in November Boughs (1888).

lg.head: Yonnondio
lg.l:
A song, a poem of itself—the word
itself a dirge

Out in Amid the wilds, the rocks, the storm
and wintry night;

A ‸To me a such misty strange tableaus, the syllables
calling up,!;

Yonnondio—I see, far in the west or north,
a limitless ravine, with plains and
mountains dark,

I see swarms of stalwart chieftains,
medicine⹀men, and warriors,

l.del:
(No picture, poem, statement, passing them
to the future,)

lg.l:
As flitting by like clouds of ghosts, they
pass and are gone in the twilight,

(Race of the woods, the landscapses free, and the
falls;

l.add: No picture, poem, statement, passing it them to the future;)
To-day gives place, and fades—the cities farms ‸factories settlements, fade,

lg.l:
A muffled sonorous sound, a wailing ‸word ‸is borne
through the air ‸for a moment,
Then blank and gone and still, and utterly lost.
